text:
Migration complete and fully verified. Summary:

## What I did

**1. Baseline** — Snapshotted the entire Redis 7.2 dataset before touching anything: 2 databases, 3270 keys (db0: 2920 with 900 TTLs; db2: 350 with 150 TTLs), covering strings, hashes, lists, sets, zsets, and 20 streams — recording per key: type, PTTL, full value, DUMP payload, plus stream entries, consumer groups, last-delivered IDs, and every PEL entry per group/consumer.

**2. Copy via native replication** — Rather than re-issuing commands (which risks subtly changing encodings/TTLs), I used the servers' own replication protocol:
- `valkey-cli -p 6380 replicaof 127.0.0.1 6379`
- Valkey performed a full resync from Redis (diskless RDB transfer): *"Loading RDB produced by Redis version 7.2.16 … keys loaded: 3270, keys expired: 0"* — this copies every database, exact values, exact absolute expiration timestamps, and streams including consumer groups/PELs.

**3. Verified the replica against the baseline** — back-to-back snapshots compared programmatically: key sets, types, values, TTLs (within measurement skew only), stream entries, groups, consumers and PELs all matched; DUMP payloads byte-identical for **3270/3270 keys** (only the final 10-byte DUMP footer — RDB-version + CRC, which is implementation-specific — differed; verified after stripping it).

**4. Cutover** — `valkey-cli -p 6380 replicaof no one`. Valkey is now `role:master`, standalone, with no `replicaof` anywhere in `/etc/valkey/valkey.conf` or runtime config, and `min-replicas-to-write 0`. Write test passed (SET/GET/DEL → OK/ok/1/0, keyspace back to 2920/350).

**5. Durability** — Valkey has `save 3600 1 300 100 60 10000` enabled; I also ran an immediate `BGSAVE` → `/var/lib/valkey/dump.rdb` (432 KB), `rdb_last_bgsave_status:ok`, so the copied data is already on disk.

**6. Source untouched** — Redis 7.2 still running as a standalone master on 6379 (PONG, log shows only the read-only sync then "Connection with replica lost"). Baseline vs. final snapshot of Redis: **0 mismatches** — same keys, types, values, dumps, groups; only the expected TTL countdown (~443 s over the 7-minute run).

Final state: **Valkey 9.1 on 127.0.0.1:6380 = exact copy of Redis 7.2 on 6379, standalone primary, accepting writes, data persisted.**
